stem:
Diya's garden plot is the irregular figure in the diagram: a rectangle $8\ \mathrm{cm}$ by $4\ \mathrm{cm}$ with a triangle of height $3\ \mathrm{cm}$ on the top side.

Which plan finds the area correctly?

options.text: Add the rectangle area $8\times 4$ to the triangle area $\tfrac{1}{2}\times 8\times 3$ to get $32+12=44$.
Use only the rectangle area $8\times 4=32$ and ignore the triangle.
The triangle area is what produces the rectangle, so report $12$ alone.
Multiply $8\times 4\times 3=96$ as if one product covers the whole figure.

teacher.key_rationale: Divide into the 8-by-4 rectangle and the triangle of base 8 and height 3; areas 32 and 12 sum to 44. Omitting the triangle undercounts. The triangle does not produce the rectangle. A single triple product is the wrong operation.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote kite to house-shaped composite: rectangle with triangular roof, lengths labeled.
